div.head: Hl 7[a]
div.ab: Gif man oþrum mæn feoh forstele, ⁊ se agend hit eft ætfó, geteme to cynges sele, gif he mæge, ⁊ þone ætgebrenge þe him sealde;
Gif man oþrum mæn feoh forstele, ⁊ se agend hit eft ætfó, geteme to cynges sele, gif he mæge, ⁊ þone ætgebrenge þe him sealde;
Gif man oþrum mæn feoh forstele, ⁊ se agend hit eft ætfo, geteme to cynges sele gif he mæge, ⁊ þone æt gebrenge þe him sealde.

Wenn einer einem andern Manne [bewegliches] Gut stiehlt, und es späterhin dieser Eigenthümer [im Anefang] fasst, [so] ziehe [der verklagte Besitzer] die Gewähr zur Königshalle, wenn er kann, indem er denjenigen herbeibringt, welcher es ihm verkauft hat;

If someone steals [movable] property from another man, and afterwards this owner seizes it [by attachment], [then] let [the accused possessor] vouch to warranty at the king’s hall, if he can, by bringing forward the one who sold it to him;
If one man steals property from another, and the owner afterwards reclaims it, he [who is in possession] shall bring it to the king’s residence, if he can, and produce the man who sold it him.

If anyone steals the property of another man, and the owner afterwards attaches it, he [the accused] is to vouch to warranty at the king’s hall, if he can, and produce him who sold it to him; if he cannot do that, he is to relinquish it, and the owner to succeed to it.
If a person steals property from another person, and the owner afterwards takes possession of it, let him [the accused] vouch in the king’s hall, if he is able, and bring him who sold it to him.
div.note: Whitelock translates Hl 7 as one clause, which the sheet divides into rows 7[a], 7[b]; her translation of the whole is given here, in the first row.

note.seg: Dieselben technischen Ausdrücke auch u. 16 für Verkauf, Anefang (s. d. Gl 1d. 17), Gewährzug, vor Gericht stellen, Gericht (s. d. Gl 4e), verloren geben
The same technical terms also below 16 for sale, attachment (see that word in Gl 1d. 17), vouching to warranty, producing in court, court (see that word in Gl 4e), giving up as lost

Zweifellos bestand auch im Kernlande Kent, bevor London von diesem abhing, ein königliches Gericht, vermutlich z. B. in Canterbury. Nicht jeder Viehkauf braucht in London erfolgt zu sein; gegen Hermann Mobiliarvindik. 149. [Man bessere im Gl Anefang 20b: ‘vors Königsgericht; Hl 7; nach London 16, 1’]. Schon hier wird Gewährzug königlicher Gerichtsbarkeit vorbehalten; s. Gl Anefang 20c

There was undoubtedly a royal court in the core territory of Kent as well, before London was dependent on it, presumably e.g. at Canterbury. Not every purchase of cattle need have taken place in London; against Hermann Mobiliarvindik. 149. [In Gl Anefang 20b correct to: ‘before the king’s court; Hl 7; to London 16, 1’]. Already here vouching to warranty is reserved to royal jurisdiction; see Gl Anefang 20c

Stellen des Gewähren vor Gericht erklärt für eine Neuerung Brunner II 502; ebd. 20e. — Aus der Nichterwähnung des Ureigeneids des Beklagten möchte ich nicht mit H. Meyer Publizität 14 damalige Nichtexistenz folgern: jener mochte dem volkstümlichen Gericht gehören

Brunner II 502 declares the production of the warrantor in court to be an innovation; ibid. 20e. — From the fact that the defendant’s oath of original ownership is not mentioned I would not, with H. Meyer Publizität 14, infer that it did not exist at that time: it may have belonged to the popular court
More literally ‘attaches’; cf. cap. 16 § 1 below; Ine, cap. 53, etc (befo).

note.label: vouch
note.seg: Whitelock, English Historical Documents, uses the term ‘vouch to warranty,’ which seems redundant. ‘Vouch’ is defined in Black’s Law Dictionary as ‘to call upon witness to give warrantee of title, to substantiate with evidence.’ Here it stands for the process of bringing the person from whom you purchased property or goods as a witness that the sale was legitimate. See discussion in Sir Frederick Pollock and Frederic Maitland, The History of English Law Before the Time of Edward I (London: Cambridge University Press, 1968), 58–60.
